# wallix.bastion.notification

Manage notifications on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a notification on a WALLIX Bastion.
- A notification sends an email to a list of addresses when some events happen on the Bastion.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_notification` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the notification. |
| <a id="parameter-destination"></a>**destination** | `str` | Email addresses the notification is sent to, separated by commas.<br>Required when the notification does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state). |
| <a id="parameter-enabled"></a>**enabled** | `bool` | Whether the notification is sent.<br>Required when the notification does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state). |
| <a id="parameter-events"></a>**events** | `list / elements=str` | Events that trigger the notification. Order does not matter.<br>When set, replaces all the events of the notification. Use `[]` to remove all events.<br><br>Choices: `cx_equipment`, `daily_reporting`, `disk_space_critical`, `external_storage_full`, `filesystem_full`, `integrity_error`, `licence_notifications`, `new_fingerprint`, `password_expired`, `pattern_found`, `primary_cx_failed`, `raid_error`, `rdp_outcxn_found`, `rdp_pattern_found`, `rdp_process_found`, `secondary_cx_failed`, `sessionlog_purge`, `watchdog_notifications`, `wrong_fingerprint` |
| <a id="parameter-language"></a>**language** | `str` | Language of the notification.<br>Required when the notification does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Choices: `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ru` |
| <a id="parameter-notification-name"></a>**notification_name** | `str` / required | Name of the notification. Identifies the notification on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the notification should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-type"></a>**type** | `str` | How the notification is sent. The Bastion only supports `email`.<br>Required when the notification does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Choices: `email` |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- The notification is looked up by [`notification_name`](#parameter-notification-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Mail the operations team about disk and RAID problems
  wallix.bastion.notification:
    notification_name: ops-mail
    description: Mail the operations team
    enabled: true
    type: email
    destination: ops@example.com,oncall@example.com
    language: en
    events: [disk_space_critical, filesystem_full, raid_error]

- name: Pause a notification
  wallix.bastion.notification:
    notification_name: ops-mail
    enabled: false

- name: Remove a notification
  wallix.bastion.notification:
    notification_name: ops-mail
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the notification already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["events"]` |
| <a id="return-notification"></a>**notification** | `dict` | The notification as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected notification. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-notification) |

<a id="sample-notification"></a>

### Sample of `notification`

```yaml
description: Mail the operations team
destination: ops@example.com,oncall@example.com
enabled: true
events:
- disk_space_critical
- filesystem_full
- raid_error
id: 1a0f76994902158e005056b66c8b
language: en
notification_name: ops-mail
type: email
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/notifications/1a0f76994902158e005056b66c8b
```
